title: Find a cool place near you: the Koele Kaart
summary: Rotterdams Weerwoord's Koele Kaart (cool map) shows places to cool down during hot days, such as parks, libraries and museums, plus the nearest drinking water points.
details: Open the map on your phone and search from your own location
Shows indoor places to cool off and nearby drinking water points
Made by Rotterdams Weerwoord, the city's climate adaptation programme

title: Refill your bottle for free at a public water tap
summary: Rotterdam has more than 120 free public drinking water taps across its neighbourhoods. Useful on any day out, essential on hot ones.
details: More than 120 water taps spread over the city's neighbourhoods
Find the nearest one on the city's interactive map (kaartlaag.rotterdam.nl/watertappunten)

sources.title: Gemeente Rotterdam: Watertappunten op de kaart

title: Check on older neighbours when the Heat Plan is on
summary: When the national heat plan (Nationaal Hitteplan) is active, RIVM asks everyone to look out for vulnerable people around them: older people, babies and people with a chronic illness.
details: Ask vulnerable people how they are doing
Encourage them to drink more than usual, even if they say they are not thirsty
Advise doing activities before 12:00 or after 18:00
Watch for headaches and dizziness; never leave young children in a parked car

sources.title: Rijksoverheid: Wat kan ik doen tegen de hitte?

title: Follow KNMI heat warnings (code yellow, orange, red)
summary: The national weather service KNMI issues heat warnings when temperatures get dangerous. Check the KNMI app or website before planning a hot day.
details: Code yellow: the Nationaal Hitteplan is active, or one day of 35 °C or more
Code orange or red: 3 days in a row from 34 °C, 2 days from 36 °C, or 1 day from 38 °C
The KNMI app shows the warnings and the new 'hittekracht' heat index

title: Subsidy for outdoor sun screens on your home
summary: Owners and tenants can get money back for outdoor sun shading that keeps a home cooler, through the city's climate adaptation subsidy.
details: € 62,50 per m² of sun screen, up to € 700 per building
Apply at least 8 weeks before the work starts
Open to owners, tenants, VvE's and non-profit organisations

title: Check the air quality where you are: Luchtmeetnet
summary: Luchtmeetnet shows measured and expected air quality for your location, including Rotterdam's DCMR measuring stations. DCMR points residents here.
details: Air quality on your location for the next 24 hours
Five levels: goed, matig, onvoldoende, slecht, zeer slecht
Also on Teletekst page 711

sources.title: Rijksoverheid: Informatie over luchtverontreiniging en smog

title: What to do on a smog day
summary: RIVM advises people who are sensitive to poor air to cut back on exertion during smog. Sensitive means people with lung or heart conditions, diabetes, children, older people and pregnant women.
details: Limit or avoid heavy physical exertion outdoors
With summer ozone smog, stay inside when levels peak in the late afternoon and early evening
People with asthma or COPD: always carry your medication
Athletes and people doing heavy outdoor work also breathe in more

title: Report smell, smoke or dust to DCMR, day and night
summary: DCMR is the environmental agency for Rotterdam and the region. Report a bad smell, smoke or other air nuisance so they can trace the source.
details: Call 0888 333 555, day and night
Or use the online form on the DCMR website
Covers Rotterdam and 12 other municipalities in the region

title: Check the Stookwijzer before lighting a wood stove
summary: The national Stookwijzer combines wind and air quality per postcode to tell you whether burning wood today causes nuisance and pollution.
details: Yellow: burning causes nuisance and air pollution
Orange: better not to burn wood now
Red: do not burn wood
Find it at atlasleefomgeving.nl/stookwijzer

title: Insulation subsidy for owner-occupied houses
summary: Homeowners who live in their own house (eengezinswoning) can get a city subsidy for insulating roof, walls, floor or windows. Open until the end of 2027 or until the budget runs out.
details: Up to € 2.000 per home, or € 2.200 if you do 2 or more measures at once
Home built in 1992 or earlier, with a WOZ value under € 477.000 (1 January 2024)
At least 2 poorly insulated parts: roof, facade, floor or windows
Apply up to and including 31 December 2027, or until the money runs out

sources.title: Gemeente Rotterdam: Subsidie isolatie eengezinswoningen aanvragen

title: Subsidy for sustainable solar panels
summary: Residents, businesses and organisations in Rotterdam can get a subsidy per solar panel when they choose an approved sustainable brand.
details: € 100, € 75 or € 50 per panel, depending on the panel
Residents apply within 12 weeks after installation
First come, first served; open until 31 December 2026

sources.title: Gemeente Rotterdam: Subsidie duurzame zonnepanelen aanvragen

title: Free energy handyman if your energy bill is hard to pay
summary: Rotterdammers who struggle to pay their energy bill can get a free 'energieklusser' at home who fits LED bulbs, draught strips and radiator foil.
details: Free: the city pays all costs
Saves around € 200 a year, according to the city
Call 14 010 and choose option 4, or visit a Vraagwijzer location
The city no longer gives out free insulating curtains

title: Free advice from the Rotterdam energy desk
summary: The Energieloket helps homeowners and tenants with questions on insulation, solar panels, heat pumps, subsidies and saving energy.
details: Call 088 525 4110 or email rotterdam@regionaalenergieloket.nl (weekdays 9:00 to 17:30)
Walk-in at Westersingel 32A: first Tuesday and third Thursday of the month, 17:00 to 20:00
Free online 'woningscan' to see which measures suit your home

title: Subsidy for rain barrels, green gardens and green roofs
summary: The city pays towards measures that hold rainwater: extra water storage, more green in your garden, on your roof or facade, and disconnecting your downpipe.
details: € 250 per extra 500 litres of water storage (minimum 500 litres)
€ 10 per extra m² of green (minimum 20 m²), plus a bonus per plant
Apply at least 8 weeks before you start; decision within 8 weeks
Questions: call 14 010

title: Water on the street or in your basement: who to call
summary: After a cloudburst, report water on the street or in your basement to the city. Canals, ditches and water levels belong to the water board for your area.
details: Street or basement: call 14 010, or report in the MeldR app (its map shows existing reports)
North of the Maas: Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard, 010 453 72 00
West Rotterdam: Delfland, 015 260 81 08
South of the Maas: Hollandse Delta, 0900 200 50 05
Keeping your own home and plot dry is your own responsibility: sandbags, a submersible pump, valuables up high

sources.title: Hoogheemraadschap van Schieland en de Krimpenerwaard: Veelgestelde vragen bij veel regen

title: Living outside the dikes: Noordereiland, Kop van Feijenoord, Scheepvaartkwartier
summary: About 40,000 Rotterdammers live outside the main flood defences. In storm season these areas can flood at high water, and the city warns residents and puts out sandbags.
details: Storm season runs from 1 October to 15 April
From 2,40 m above NAP the city informs Noordereiland residents
From 2,80 m above NAP the city places pallets with a limited number of filled sandbags on Noordereiland
Put sandbags or barriers at doors, park your car higher up, move valuables upstairs, switch off electricity

title: What the city does at high water, and what you do
summary: The Maeslantkering storm barrier closes when the forecast reaches 3,00 m above NAP. About 24 hours before expected high water the city starts its protocol, including warnings and notices to move cars.
details: Make your home watertight with sandbags or flood boards
Move belongings to a higher floor and your car to higher ground
If water threatens your home, shut off the main switches and valves for electricity, water and gas

title: Check river and sea water levels: Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo
summary: Rijkswaterstaat's Waterinfo shows current, expected and historical water levels on the main rivers and the coast, on a map with tables and graphs.
details: Current and forecast water heights for the state waters
Look up a measuring station near you on the map

title: Prepare your home for a flood
summary: Rotterdams Weerwoord lists practical steps for homes in low-lying areas, from sandbags and water barriers to a waterproof box for important papers.
details: Keep sandbags or water barriers for doors and windows
Store important documents in a waterproof container
Place electrical appliances higher up and know your evacuation route
Check whether your insurance covers flooding

sources.title: Rotterdams Weerwoord: Bereid je huis voor op overstroming

title: Check how high the water could get at your address: Overstroom ik?
summary: The national flood information site shows how high water could rise in your area if a flood happens, and how to prepare. Run by Rijkswaterstaat, the safety regions, the water boards and two ministries.
details: Enter your location to see the water height in your area during a flood
Step-by-step advice on how to prepare
An initiative of Rijkswaterstaat, the veiligheidsregio's, the waterschappen, the ministries of I&W and J&V, and the Deltaprogramma

title: Free bus, tram and metro for AOW-age Rotterdammers
summary: Rotterdam residents who have reached AOW pension age can travel free on RET bus, tram and metro off-peak.
details: The travel product itself is free; a personal OV-chipkaart costs € 7,50 (valid 5 years)
Valid weekdays from 9:00 and all day at weekends and on public holidays
Apply online; processed within 3 weeks

sources.title: Gemeente Rotterdam: Gratis OV voor AOW-gerechtigden aanvragen

title: Free bike parking at Rotterdam Centraal
summary: Most bike parking around Rotterdam Centraal is free and open 24/7, so cycling to the train is easy.
details: Stationsplein (underground): 5.190 places, 4.180 of them free
Stationssingel (north side): 1.700+ places, free, max 14 days
Conradstraat: 1.000 places, free, max 4 weeks
Bikes parked outside racks and garages are removed

title: Take your bike on the metro off-peak
summary: RET lets you bring a bike on the metro outside rush hours, so you can combine cycling and metro for longer trips.
details: Weekdays between 9:00 and 16:00 and after 18:30; all day at weekends
Walk your bike in the station; max 2 bikes per entrance
Staff can refuse bikes when it is very busy; wheelchairs go first

title: Find a public charging point for your electric car
summary: Rotterdam has more than 3,400 public charging points. The city's location map shows the ones already placed and the ones being processed.
details: Map of placed and planned charging points: viewer.evmaps.nl/rotterdam (linked by the city)
Or use the E-Flux app, the ANWB Onderweg app or your charge card provider's app
New charging points are placed based on data

title: Drop off bulky waste and reusable items for free at a milieupark
summary: Rotterdam has 6 milieuparken where residents can bring waste, bulky items and usable second-hand goods for free.
details: Free for Rotterdam residents
Your postcode or number plate is checked at the gate
Closed on major public holidays; closes at 15:00 on 5, 24 and 31 December

title: Separate food and garden waste (gfe+t)
summary: In more and more Rotterdam neighbourhoods you can put vegetable, fruit, food and garden waste in a separate container. You get a notice when your area starts.
details: Collect peels, coffee grounds, eggshells, leftovers and wilted flowers in a small kitchen bin
Empty it into your gfe+t container every few days
The city empties gfe+t containers every two weeks

sources.title: Gemeente Rotterdam: Groente-, fruit- en etensresten en tuinafval

title: Worn-out clothes and textiles go in a textile container
summary: Even torn or worn textiles are recycled. Rotterdam has 237 textile containers, or bring textiles to a milieupark.
details: Accepted: worn clothing, shoes, curtains, sheets, cuddly toys, even single socks
237 textile containers across the city
Items in good condition go to kringloopwinkels via the milieupark

title: Book a free bulky waste pickup
summary: The city picks up bulky waste at your door for free. Book online or by phone and put it out on the morning of pickup.
details: Free for Rotterdam residents
Book online ('Grofvuil laten ophalen') or call 14 010
Put it out before 8:00 on pickup day, not the evening before (you can be fined)
Pieces max 1 metre and 30 kilo each; no more than one parking space in total
Construction and demolition waste is not accepted

title: Get things repaired for free at Repair Café Rotterdam Noord
summary: Volunteers help you fix broken appliances, furniture, bikes, objects and clothing, so they don't end up in the bin.
details: Every second Saturday of the month, 10:00 to 12:00; they stop at 12:00, so come on time
Next dates: 10 October and 14 November 2026
Het Klooster Oude Noorden, Ruivenstraat 81, 3036 DD Rotterdam
Repairs are free; a voluntary contribution is welcome

sources.title: Rotterdam Circulair (Gemeente Rotterdam): Repaircafé Rotterdam Noord
